dedupe_keys.name: cape town day zero drought 2017 to 2018 how transparency and behaviour change halved water use siwi

description: This case study is a SIWI feature on how Cape Town avoided Day Zero, the day the city would turn off the taps, during the drought that sounded its alarm in the summer of 2017. It describes restrictions that fell to 50 litres per person per day in 2018 and stood at 105 litres more than a year later, spring water collection points in Newlands, grey-water reuse by households, and the finding that transparency, information and behavioural change drove an effort across all sectors. Consumption dropped from 1,200 to 1,500 million litres a day at pre-drought summer peaks to about 650 million litres by November 2019, with figures starting to creep up again. A city water and waste services mayoral committee member says the drought taught the city to take residents along. SIWI, a water governance think tank, wrote it for a general audience. Coverage: one city over 2017 to 2019, with quoted figures, not a data series. Access: free web page; licence not stated. Caveats: it is a journalistic account with interviews, and consumption numbers are quoted, not tabulated. It informs drought demand-management scenarios, restriction-level design and behavioural response modelling for urban water supply, and complements other Cape Town studies not yet catalogued.
